newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta consolidates vs mark after heady gains.
newsitem.headline: Peseta consolidates vs mark after heady gains.

text.p: The peseta eased off early levels against the mark in afternoon trade on Monday in what traders saw as an effort to consolidate after a strong run following the break of the key 84.00 per mark barrier on Friday.
By 1610 GMT, the peseta was trading at 83.47/48 after touching 83.35 earlier in the session and compared with early trading levels of 83.37/40 per mark.
"It was quite a quiet session with a little bit of profit taking and consolidation after Friday's strong moves," said one trader.
"However, the peseta remains well bid and we should see some more appreciation in coming sessions," he said.

Traders said the Bank of Spain had been absent from the currency market on Monday. The central bank had been intervening for some months to hold the peseta above the key 84.00 per mark region until Friday.
Spain's December CPI data due on Wednesday and the results of the Bank of Spain's regular repurchase auction will provide some focus for the Spanish currency, traders said.

Although most analysts expect the central bank will await more inflation data before deciding on the next interest rate cut, a handful say peseta strength will prompt a 25 basis point cut on Thursday.
